products.name: Alteryx AI
products.note: Analytics automation with AI; data blending; workflow governance; self-service analytics risk

reading.body:
Alteryx provides analytics automation software that integrates AI for data blending and self-service analytics, positioning itself in the data preparation layer rather than model development or inference.

The distinction matters for AI infrastructure. Data quality and preparation consume significant engineering effort before any model sees input, yet the compute requirements here are modest compared to training or deployment. Alteryx sits upstream of the inference path, automating the human work of structuring raw data into usable form. This belongs to the broader stack, but it is not where compute constraints tighten.

The data covers a single product line and does not specify deployment scale, customer base, infrastructure needs, or power consumption. It identifies what Alteryx does, not the resource requirements that would connect it to the binding constraints on AI scaling. The category label "Data & Analytics AI" is broad enough that the actual role in any particular AI project—whether critical or peripheral—remains unclear from this entry alone.

profile_text.body:
Alteryx describes itself as an agentic analytics and automation company that helps organizations turn complex data into trusted insights, decisions, and action with AI-ready datasets, governed business logic, and visual workflows. Its site centers on Alteryx One, a platform for automating data workflows, reducing manual work, and delivering AI-powered insights, with integrations to Snowflake, Databricks, and BI tools. The company says Alteryx One combines automated operations and accelerated decisions through automated business logic, low-code tools, AI assistance, and built-in governance. It also states that workflows and agents are visible, understandable, repeatable, and auditable, and that agentic AI does not get an exception to VURA.

The company's AI positioning includes Alteryx AI, described as involving analytics automation with AI, data blending, workflow governance, and self-service analytics risk. The site claims Alteryx can "100X your decision making" and says it is rated a leader across multiple 2026 analyst evaluations for making advanced analytics and AI trustworthy at enterprise scale. It cites McLaren Racing as a user of Alteryx AI data analytics for race performance and car design, and mentions a Summer 2026 Release Webinar on September 24, a Virtual Summit with Steve Nouri, Nezrin Noushad, and Anthony Alteirac, and a session with MIT's Dr. Barb Wixom and CEO Andy MacMillan.

Alteryx was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Irvine.
